== Biography ==
Caroline Hill Rigby Glasgow was born on 8 Feb 1845 at Kensington, London, England. She was living with her parents,  John Glasgow, of Scotland and Ann, at Stretford, Lancashire in 1851. <ref>"England and Wales Census, 1851," database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:SGYD-7YN : 24 July 2016), Caroline Glasgow in household of Ann Glasgow, Stretford, Lancashire, England; citing Stretford, Lancashire, England, p. 2, from "1851 England, Scotland and Wales census," database and images, findmypast (http://www.findmypast.com : n.d.); citing PRO HO 107, The National Archives of the UK, Kew, Surrey.</ref> 

Caroline married William Henry Tate in 1863 at Liverpool, Lancashire.<ref>"England and Wales Marriage Registration Index, 1837-2005," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:2DVK-2DM : 13 December 2014), Caroline Hill Rigby Glasgow, 1863; from “England & Wales Marriages, 1837-2005,” database, findmypast (http://www.findmypast.com : 2012); citing 1863, quarter 4, vol. 8B, p. 589, Liverpool, Lancashire, England, General Register Office, Southport, England.</ref>

In 1871 she was living with her husband and children.<ref>"England and Wales Census, 1871", database with images, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VRNH-XS7 : 24 July 2015), Caroline H R Tate in entry for William H Tate, 1871.</ref>

She died in 14 Dec 1927 at Rhuddlan, Denbighshire, Wales. <ref>"England and Wales Death Registration Index 1837-2007," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:QVH8-HCWT : 4 September 2014), Caroline H R Tate, 1927; from "England & Wales Deaths, 1837-2006," database, findmypast (http://www.findmypast.com : 2012); citing Death, St. Asaph, Denbighshire, Wales, General Register Office, Southport, England.</ref>

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-960]] is assessed at 47% (possible). The father’s biography describes adoption, but the cited secondary account checked on22 October 2026 says daughter without that qualification; biological paternity therefore remains unresolved at47%.

This percentage concerns biological fatherhood, distinct from the well-supported family daughter role. The adoption description is retained as an unverified report; Burke’s underlying 2003 volume and the original birth/census entries have not been newly inspected.
